title: Eternity in Their Hearts
subtitle: Ecclesiastes in Poems & Pictures
author: Timothy Holt
beforeYouBegin:
Ecclesiastes begins with a single word said twice over, vanity, a breath, and then looks hard at everything a person might chase: gardens and pools, silver and gold, wisdom itself. In between: the wind going around, rivers running into a sea that is never full, a time to weep and a time to dance, a threefold cord, bread cast on the waters, an almond tree in blossom, and a silver cord and a golden bowl.

This book walks through it in thirty-six short poems, in four parts. Each poem sits beside a picture and under a single line of Scripture. The pictures stay with the things the Preacher noticed—a lamp just blown out, a heap of field stones, a loaf and a cup—and leave the faces to your imagination.

The poems are not the Bible. They are one reader's response to it. Open the book of Ecclesiastes alongside this book, and let the real words have the last word.

paintings.title: the preacher
paintings.epigraph: “The words of the Preacher, the son of David, king in Jerusalem”
paintings.poem:
he had everything
a person could want.

gold in the storerooms.
singers in the hall.
a city at his feet.

and one evening
he sat down
and began to write
about why
none of it was enough.

it's an odd way
to begin a book of the Bible.

it may also be
the most honest.
paintings.reflectionPrompt: Take a slow breath and read the final line again: “it may also be the most honest.” How would you walk through the next hour differently if you carried that truth with you?
paintings.zh_poem:
他拥有一切
一个人可能想要。

储藏室里有黄金。
大厅里的歌手。
一座城就在他的脚下。

和一个晚上
他坐下来
并开始写
关于为什么
这些都还不够。

这是一种奇怪的方式
开始一本圣经。

也可能是
最诚实的。
paintings.zh_reflectionPrompt: 缓缓吸了口气，又读了一遍最后一行：“这也可能是最诚实的。”如果你带着这个真理，你会如何以不同的方式度过接下来的一个小时？
paintings.zh_epigraph: “耶路撒冷王大卫儿子传道者的话”

paintings.title: breath
paintings.epigraph: “all is vanity.”
paintings.poem:
the old word underneath
is closer to breath.

a puff of warm air
on a cold morning.
there, and then not.

that's the house.
that's the harvest.
that's the name
carved over the gate.

he's not saying
nothing matters.

he's saying
nothing lasts
the way you hoped.

so notice it
while it's warm.
paintings.reflectionPrompt: Think of a season when you knew the feeling of “the old word underneath is closer to breath.” Looking through the lens of Ecclesiastes 1:2, what does it mean to discover that “so notice it while it's warm”?
paintings.zh_poem:
下面的旧词
更接近呼吸。

一股暖风
在一个寒冷的早晨。
有，然后没有。

这就是房子。
这就是收获。
这就是名字
刻在门上。

他不是说
没有什么重要的。

他在说
没有什么可以持久
正如你所希望的那样。

所以注意它
趁天气暖和的时候。
paintings.zh_reflectionPrompt: 回想一下某个季节，您体会到“下面的旧词更接近呼吸”的感觉。从传道书 1:2 的角度来看，发现“趁天热的时候要留意”是什么意思？
paintings.zh_epigraph: “一切都是虚空。”

paintings.title: the earth remains
paintings.epigraph: “One generation goes, and another generation comes; but the earth remains forever.”
paintings.poem:
someone's grandfather
walked these terraces.
his grandfather
set these stones.

the olive trees
have outlived them all
and look
no older.

the sun comes up, goes down,
and hurries back around.

it was here
before your name.
it will be here
after.

there's a strange comfort
in being small.
paintings.reflectionPrompt: Look closely at the deep roots of the tree in this painting (Ecclesiastes 1:4–5)—if you could leave one anxious weight beside it today, what would you set down?
paintings.zh_poem:
某人的祖父
走过这些露台。
他的祖父
设置这些石头。

橄榄树
已经比他们都长寿了
看看
没有老。

太阳升起，落下，
然后赶紧回去。

就在这里
在你的名字之前。
它将在这里
之后。

有一种奇怪的安慰
在很小的时候。
paintings.zh_reflectionPrompt: 仔细观察这幅画中树的深深根部（传道书 1：4-5）——如果今天你可以在它旁边留下一个令人焦虑的重物，你会放下什么？
paintings.zh_epigraph: “一代人过去了，一代人又来了；但地球却永远长存。”

paintings.title: the wind and the sea
paintings.epigraph: “All the rivers run into the sea, yet the sea is not full.”
paintings.poem:
the wind goes south,
turns north,
and comes back
to where it started.

every river empties itself
into the sea,
and the sea is never full.

he watched it
the way you watch
your own life:

all that running.
all that pouring.
and the wide water
still asking.

some hungers
nothing under the sun
was made to fill.
paintings.reflectionPrompt: Let your eyes rest on the brushwork and light around the moving water: what quiet prayer rises in you when you read, “some hungers nothing under the sun was made to fill”?
paintings.zh_poem:
风向南，
转向北，
然后回来
到它开始的地方。

每条河流都会自行排空
进入大海，
大海永远不会满。

他看了
你观看的方式
你自己的生活：

所有这些运行。
倾盆大雨。
和宽阔的水面
还在问。

一些饥饿
阳光下什么也没有
被用来填充。
paintings.zh_reflectionPrompt: 让你的目光停留在流动的水面周围的笔触和光线上：当你读到“有些人的饥饿在阳光下无法得到满足”时，你内心会升起什么样的安静的祈祷？
paintings.zh_epigraph: “江河皆入海，海却未满”。

paintings.title: nothing new
paintings.epigraph: “there is no new thing under the sun.”
paintings.poem:
the potter
thinks he's made
a new kind of jar.

then he digs a garden
and turns up its twin
in pieces,

someone else's hands,
someone else's morning,
long ago.

whatever road
you're on tonight,
someone walked it
before you

and left
a path.
paintings.reflectionPrompt: Linger with the movement in “nothing new” (Ecclesiastes 1:9–10) from “the potter thinks he's made a new kind of jar” to “whatever road you're on tonight, someone walked it before you and left a path”—where do you find yourself along that arc today?
paintings.zh_poem:
陶工
认为他已经做到了
一种新的罐子。

然后他挖了一个花园
并出现了它的双胞胎
分成碎片，

别人的手，
别人的早晨，
很久以前。

无论哪条路
今晚你在
有人走过它
在你之前

然后离开了
一条路径。
paintings.zh_reflectionPrompt: 沉浸在“没什么新鲜事”（传道书 1：9-10）中的运动中，从“陶工认为他做了一种新的罐子”到“无论你今晚走在哪条路上，有人在你前面走过，留下了一条路”——今天你发现自己在这条弧线上的什么地方？
paintings.zh_epigraph: “太阳底下并无新鲜事。”

paintings.title: chasing after wind
paintings.epigraph: “all is vanity and a chasing after wind.”
paintings.poem:
go out on a windy day
and catch a handful.

close your fist.
open it.
nothing.

he tried it
with wisdom,
with pleasure,
with work,
and told us plainly:

the wind
is not for keeping.

it's for
feeling on your face.
paintings.reflectionPrompt: Notice how “chasing after wind” (Ecclesiastes 1:14) arrives at: “it's for feeling on your face.” Who in your life is walking a hard stretch of road today and needs you to share this grace with them?
paintings.zh_poem:
有风的日子出去
并抓住一把。

握紧你的拳头。
打开它。
没有什么。

他尝试过
用智慧，
很高兴，
与工作，
并明确地告诉我们：

风
不是为了保存。

这是为了
感觉在你脸上。
paintings.zh_reflectionPrompt: 请注意“捕风”（传道书 1:14）是如何演变而来的：“是为了在脸上感觉。”今天，你生命中的哪些人正走在艰难的道路上，需要你与他们分享这份恩典？
paintings.zh_epigraph: “一切都是虚空，都是捕风。”

paintings.title: great works
paintings.epigraph: “I made myself great works. I built myself houses. I planted myself vineyards.”
paintings.poem:
houses.
vineyards.
gardens and parks.
pools to water
a forest of fruit trees.

and the word he keeps using:
myself.
myself.
myself.

then he walked through it all
and looked.

no profit,
he said.
wind.

the finest garden
in Jerusalem,
and the man who planted it
standing in the middle,
hungry.
paintings.reflectionPrompt: What if the most important thing you remember before tonight is the quiet lesson of Ecclesiastes 2:4–11: “the finest garden in Jerusalem, and the man who planted it standing in the middle, hungry”?
paintings.zh_poem:
房屋。
葡萄园。
花园和公园。
水池到水
果树森林

他一直用的词是：
我自己。
我。
我。

然后他经历了这一切
并看了看。

没有利润，
他说。
风。

最好的花园
在耶路撒冷，
和种植它的人
站在中间，
饿了。
paintings.zh_reflectionPrompt: 如果今晚之前你记得的最重要的事情是《传道书》2:4-11 中的静谧教训：“耶路撒冷最好的园子，栽种园子的人却饿着肚子站在中间”，那又怎样呢？
paintings.zh_epigraph: “我为自己创造了伟大的作品。我为自己建造了房屋。我为自己种植了葡萄园。”

paintings.title: from the hand of God
paintings.epigraph: “This also I saw, that it is from the hand of God.”
paintings.poem:
after the palace,
after the gold,

here's what he found:

bread.
a cup.
honest work
and the pleasure of it.

nothing better, he says.

not a consolation prize.
a gift.

it comes
from the hand of God,

and you can
hold it
in yours.
paintings.reflectionPrompt: Imagine standing inside this frame beside the daily loaf broken in the hand: what hurry or noise in your week begins to fade when you hear, “it comes from the hand of God, and you can hold it in yours”?
paintings.zh_poem:
到了宫殿之后，
黄金之后，

这是他的发现：

面包。
一杯。
诚实做事
以及其中的乐趣。

没有什么比这更好的了，他说。

不是安慰奖。
一份礼物。

它来了
来自上帝之手，

你可以
握住它
在你的。
paintings.zh_reflectionPrompt: 想象一下，站在这个框架内，旁边是每天手中破碎的面包：当你听到“它来自上帝的手，你可以把它握在手中”时，你一周中的什么匆忙或噪音开始消失？
paintings.zh_epigraph: “我也看到，这是出自上帝之手。”

paintings.title: a season
paintings.epigraph: “a time to plant, and a time to pluck up that which is planted”
paintings.poem:
a time to plant.
a time to pull up.

we want
every season
to be spring,
every door
to be opening.

but the field knows.
it rests.
it gives.
it waits under frost
without complaint.

you're not behind.
you're not broken.

you may just be
in a different month
than you wanted.
paintings.reflectionPrompt: Read the closing words aloud in the stillness: “you may just be in a different month than you wanted.” What part of your heart feels most searched or comforted by Ecclesiastes 3:1–2 right now?
paintings.zh_poem:
播种的时间。
到了拉起的时间。

我们想要
每个季节
成为春天，
每扇门
即将开放。

但业内人士都知道。
它休息了。
它给出了。
它在霜下等待
毫无怨言。

你没有落后。
你没有崩溃。

你可能只是
在不同的月份
比你想要的。
paintings.zh_reflectionPrompt: 在寂静中大声朗读结束语：“你可能只是在与你想要的不同的月份。”现在，传道书 3:1-2 给你心灵的哪一部分带来最大的探查或安慰？
paintings.zh_epigraph: “栽种有时，拔出所栽种的有时”

paintings.title: weep and dance
paintings.epigraph: “a time to weep, and a time to laugh; a time to mourn, and a time to dance”
paintings.poem:
the same hands
that tore a garment
at the graveside

will lift
the drum again
at a wedding.

grief
keeps its own calendar
and won't be hurried.

but he wrote them
on the same line,
weeping and laughing,
mourning and dancing,

as if to say
neither one
gets the last word
forever.
paintings.reflectionPrompt: In Ecclesiastes 3:4, grace meets us right beside your own two hands: how does the closing thought—“but he wrote them on the same line, weeping and laughing, mourning and dancing, as if to say neither one gets the last word forever”—steady your footing for the road ahead?
paintings.zh_poem:
同一双手
撕破了一件衣服
在坟墓边

会举起
又是鼓声
在一场婚礼上。

悲伤
保留自己的日历
并且不会着急。

但他写了它们
在同一条线上，
又哭又笑，
哀悼和舞蹈，

仿佛在说
两者都不是
得到最后一句话
永远。
paintings.zh_reflectionPrompt: 在《传道书》3章4节中，恩典就在你的两只手旁边与我们相遇：最后的思想——“他却把它们写在同一条线上，又哭又笑，又哀又舞，好像永远没有人能说得清”——如何为你前面的路站稳脚跟？
paintings.zh_epigraph: “哭有时，笑有时；哀悼有时，跳舞有时”

paintings.title: stones
paintings.epigraph: “a time to cast away stones, and a time to gather stones together”
paintings.poem:
some years
you clear the field.

some years
you build the wall.

both
are the work.
paintings.reflectionPrompt: If today’s painting of “stones” (Ecclesiastes 3:5) hung beside the door you walk out of this morning, how would its final line—“some years you build the wall. both are the work”—shape your choices?
paintings.zh_poem:
几年
你清理场地。

几年
你建造隔离墙。

两者
是工作。
paintings.zh_reflectionPrompt: 如果今天早上你走出的门旁挂着今天的“石头”画（传道书 3:5），它的最后一句——“你建造这墙有几年了。两者都是工作”——会如何影响你的选择？
paintings.zh_epigraph: “扔石头有时，聚石头有时”

paintings.title: tear and sew
paintings.epigraph: “a time to tear, and a time to sew; a time to keep silence, and a time to speak”
paintings.poem:
there's a time
to tear it open
and a time
to stitch it closed.

a time to say
what needs saying.

a time
to sit beside someone
and say
nothing at all.

the hard part
isn't knowing how.

it's knowing
which day
this is.
paintings.reflectionPrompt: Every stop on the Pilgrim Walk shows how God meets us in ordinary places (Ecclesiastes 3:7)—where in your own home or work today does “it's knowing which day this is” ring true?
paintings.zh_poem:
有一个时间
把它撕开
和一个时间
将其缝合。

有时间说
需要说什么。

一次
坐在某人旁边
并说
什么都没有。

困难的部分
不知道如何。

它知道
哪一天
这是。
paintings.zh_reflectionPrompt: 天路历程中的每一站都展示了神如何在平常的地方与我们相遇（传道书 3:7）——今天，在你自己的家里或工作场所，“知道今天是哪一天”听起来是真的吗？
paintings.zh_epigraph: “撕裂有时，缝补有时；沉默有时，说话有时”

paintings.title: eternity in their hearts
paintings.epigraph: “He has also set eternity in their hearts”
paintings.poem:
everything beautiful
in its time, he says.

and then this:
he has set eternity
in our hearts.

that's why
the best day ends
and something in you
says wait.

we are made
for a longer time
than we have,
a larger story
than we can read
end to end.

the ache isn't a flaw.

it's a compass.
paintings.reflectionPrompt: Take a slow breath and read the final line again: “the ache isn't a flaw. it's a compass.” How would you walk through the next hour differently if you carried that truth with you?
paintings.zh_poem:
一切都美丽
他说，在当时。

然后是这个：
他设定了永恒
在我们心中。

这就是为什么
最好的一天结束了
和你身上的某些东西
说等等。

我们是被造的
更长时间
比我们拥有的，
一个更大的故事
比我们能读懂的
端到端。

疼痛不是缺陷。

这是一个指南针。
paintings.zh_reflectionPrompt: 缓慢地吸一口气，再读一遍最后一行：“疼痛不是缺陷。它是一个指南针。”如果你带着这个真理，你会如何以不同的方式度过接下来的一个小时？
paintings.zh_epigraph: “他也在他们心中安置了永恒”

paintings.title: no comforter
paintings.epigraph: “the tears of those who were oppressed, and they had no comforter”
paintings.poem:
he doesn't explain it
or make it tidy.

he sees the tears.
he sees the power,
all on one side.

and he writes it down
twice:
they had no comforter.

sometimes
the faithful thing
is to refuse
to look away.

and then,
if you can,
to be the comforter
they didn't have.
paintings.reflectionPrompt: Think of a season when you knew the feeling of “he doesn't explain it or make it tidy.” Looking through the lens of Ecclesiastes 4:1, what does it mean to discover that “and then, if you can, to be the comforter they didn't have”?
paintings.zh_poem:
他没有解释
或使其整洁。

他看到了眼泪。
他看到了力量，
全部在一侧。

他把它写下来
两次：
他们没有被子。

有时
忠实的东西
就是拒绝
移开目光。

然后，
如果可以的话
成为安慰者
他们没有。
paintings.zh_reflectionPrompt: 想象一个赛季，当你体会到“他没有解释或整理干净”的感觉时。从传道书 4:1 的角度来看，发现“然后，如果可以的话，成为他们所没有的安慰者”意味着什么？
paintings.zh_epigraph: “那些受压迫者的眼泪，他们无人安慰”

paintings.title: a handful
paintings.epigraph: “Better is a handful, with quietness, than two handfuls with labor and chasing after wind.”
paintings.poem:
one handful
and quiet.

or two handfuls
and no sleep.

he did the math
for you.
paintings.reflectionPrompt: Look closely at the quiet centerpiece of “a handful” in this painting (Ecclesiastes 4:6)—if you could leave one anxious weight beside it today, what would you set down?
paintings.zh_poem:
一把
和安静。

或两把
没有睡眠。

他算了算
为了你。
paintings.zh_reflectionPrompt: 仔细观察这幅画中安静的中心“一把”（传道书 4:6）——如果今天你可以在它旁边留下一个令人焦虑的重物，你会放什么？
paintings.zh_epigraph: “一手安静，胜过两手劳作、捕风。”

paintings.title: a threefold cord
paintings.epigraph: “a threefold cord is not quickly broken.”
paintings.poem:
two are better than one.

if one falls,
the other lifts him up.

if two lie down
on a cold night,
there's warmth
enough for both.

then he adds
a third strand
and doesn't say
what it is.

many have heard
God in it.

it would be like him
to be the strand
you can't see,
holding.
paintings.reflectionPrompt: Let your eyes rest on the brushwork and light around the quiet centerpiece of “a threefold cord”: what quiet prayer rises in you when you read, “it would be like him to be the strand you can't see, holding”?
paintings.zh_poem:
两个比一个好。

如果一个人跌倒，
另一个把他举了起来。

如果两个人躺下
在一个寒冷的夜晚，
有温暖
两者都足够了。

然后他补充道
第三股
并且没有说
它是什么。

很多人都听说过
神在其中。

就会像他一样
成为股线
你看不到，
持有。
paintings.zh_reflectionPrompt: 让你的目光停留在“三重绳索”安静中心周围的笔触和光线上：当你读到“他就像是你看不见的绳索，握着”时，你内心会升起什么样的安静祈祷？
paintings.zh_epigraph: “三股绳子不会很快折断。”

paintings.title: let your words be few
paintings.epigraph: “Therefore let your words be few.”
paintings.poem:
God is in heaven.
you are on earth.

so walk in slowly.
listen first.

you don't have to
fill the silence
to be heard.

a few words,
meant,

are better
than a thousand
you'll forget
by noon.
paintings.reflectionPrompt: Linger with the movement in “let your words be few” (Ecclesiastes 5:1–2) from “God is in heaven. you are on earth” to “a few words, meant, are better than a thousand you'll forget by noon”—where do you find yourself along that arc today?
paintings.zh_poem:
神在天上。
你在地球上。

所以慢慢地走进去。
先听听。

你不必
填补沉默
被听到。

几句话，
意思是，

更好
超过一千
你会忘记
到了中午。
paintings.zh_reflectionPrompt: 留心“少言寡语”（传道书 5：1-2）中的运动，从“神在天上，你在地上”到“几句话的意思，胜过中午你会忘记的千言万语”——今天你发现自己处于这条弧线的哪个位置？
paintings.zh_epigraph: “所以你要少说话。”

paintings.title: sweet sleep
paintings.epigraph: “The sleep of a laboring man is sweet, whether he eats little or much”
paintings.poem:
the laborer
eats his bread, lies down,
and is gone
before the lamp cools.

the rich man
lies awake,
counting.

not every blessing
can be stored.

some come only
at the end
of an honest day.

you can't buy them.
you can only
lie down and receive.
paintings.reflectionPrompt: Notice how “sweet sleep” (Ecclesiastes 5:12) arrives at: “you can only lie down and receive.” Who in your life is walking a hard stretch of road today and needs you to share this grace with them?
paintings.zh_poem:
劳动者
吃完面包，躺下，
并且消失了
在灯冷却之前。

有钱人
醒着躺着，
计数。

不是每一个祝福
可以存储。

有些人只来
最后
诚实的一天。

你买不到它们。
你只能
躺下接受。
paintings.zh_reflectionPrompt: 请注意“甜蜜的睡眠”（传道书 5:12）是如何实现的：“你只能躺下接受。”今天，你生命中的哪些人正走在艰难的道路上，需要你与他们分享这份恩典？
paintings.zh_epigraph: “劳动者无论吃得少还是吃得多，睡得都是香甜的”

paintings.title: the house of mourning
paintings.epigraph: “It is better to go to the house of mourning than to go to the house of feasting”
paintings.poem:
the party
tells you
life goes on.

the funeral
tells you
the truth:

it doesn't,
not like this,
not forever.

so go.
sit with them.
bring bread.

you'll come home quieter,
and hold the people
you love
a little longer
at the door.
paintings.reflectionPrompt: What if the most important thing you remember before tonight is the quiet lesson of Ecclesiastes 7:2: “you'll come home quieter, and hold the people you love a little longer at the door”?
paintings.zh_poem:
党
告诉你
生活还要继续。

葬礼
告诉你
真相：

事实并非如此，
不是这样的，
不是永远。

所以走吧。
和他们坐在一起。
带面包。

你回家会更安静
并抓住人民
你爱
长一点
在门口。
paintings.zh_reflectionPrompt: 如果今晚之前你记得的最重要的事情是《传道书》7:2 中安静的教训：“你回家时会更安静，并在门口多留你所爱的人一会儿”怎么办？
paintings.zh_epigraph: “去丧家，不如去宴家”

paintings.title: crackling thorns
paintings.epigraph: “For as the crackling of thorns under a pot, so is the laughter of the fool.”
paintings.poem:
loud.
bright.
snapping and popping.

and the water
never boils.
paintings.reflectionPrompt: Imagine standing inside this frame beside the quiet centerpiece of “crackling thorns”: what hurry or noise in your week begins to fade when you hear, “and the water never boils”?
paintings.zh_poem:
大声。
明亮的。
噼噼啪啪。

和水
永远不会沸腾。
paintings.zh_reflectionPrompt: 想象一下，站在这个框架内，旁边是安静的中心“噼啪作响的荆棘”：当你听到“水永远不会沸腾”时，你一周中的什么匆忙或噪音开始消失？
paintings.zh_epigraph: “因为愚人的笑声就像锅底下荆棘的噼啪声一样。”

paintings.title: the former days
paintings.epigraph: “Don’t say, “Why were the former days better than these?””
paintings.poem:
the old days
always look golden
from here.

we forget the hunger,
the fear, the long nights.

it isn't
a wise question,
he says.

not because
the past was bad,

but because
you can't live there.

the only morning
God has given you
is this one.
paintings.reflectionPrompt: Read the closing words aloud in the stillness: “the only morning God has given you is this one.” What part of your heart feels most searched or comforted by Ecclesiastes 7:10 right now?
paintings.zh_poem:
旧时光
总是看起来金色
从这里。

我们忘记了饥饿，
恐惧，漫漫长夜。

不是
一个明智的问题，
他说。

不是因为
过去很糟糕

但因为
你不能住在那里。

唯一的早晨
神已经给了你
就是这个。
paintings.zh_reflectionPrompt: 在寂静中大声朗读结束语：“上帝赐予你的唯一早晨就是这个。”现在，传道书 7 章 10 节最能触动你内心的哪一部分？
paintings.zh_epigraph: “不要说，‘为什么以前的日子比现在好？’”

paintings.title: side by side
paintings.epigraph: “In the day of prosperity be joyful, and in the day of adversity consider”
paintings.poem:
a good day?
enjoy it.
don't apologize.

a hard day?
sit down with it.
think.

God set them
side by side,
he says,
like two fields
along one road.

you'll walk through both.

and neither one
tells you
the whole story.
paintings.reflectionPrompt: In Ecclesiastes 7:14, grace meets us right beside the quiet centerpiece of “side by side”: how does the closing thought—“and neither one tells you the whole story”—steady your footing for the road ahead?
paintings.zh_poem:
美好的一天？
好好享受。
别道歉。

辛苦的一天吗？
和它坐下来。
思考。

神安排他们
并排，
他说，
就像两个领域
沿着一条路。

你将会经历这两个过程。

没有一个
告诉你
整个故事。
paintings.zh_reflectionPrompt: 在传道书 7 章 14 节中，恩典就在“肩并肩”的安静核心旁边与我们相遇：最后的思想——“没有人告诉你整个故事”——如何为你在前面的道路上站稳脚跟？
paintings.zh_epigraph: “顺境时要喜乐，逆境时要思虑”

paintings.title: upright
paintings.epigraph: “God made man upright; but they search for many schemes.”
paintings.poem:
he went looking
for the scheme of things,
the answer
under everything.

all he could say for sure
was this:

we were made
straight.

and we keep
drawing
crooked plans.

the plumb line
still hangs true.

there's still
something to come back to.
paintings.reflectionPrompt: If today’s painting of “upright” (Ecclesiastes 7:29) hung beside the door you walk out of this morning, how would its final line—“there's still something to come back to”—shape your choices?
paintings.zh_poem:
他去寻找
对于事情的计划，
答案
在一切之下。

他只能肯定地说
是这样的：

我们被创造了
直。

我们保留
绘图
歪曲的计划。

铅垂线
仍然有效。

还有
一些值得回来的事情。
paintings.zh_reflectionPrompt: 如果今天早上你走出的门旁挂着今天的“正直”（传道书 7:29）画，它的最后一句——“还有事要回来”——会如何影响你的选择？
paintings.zh_epigraph: “上帝造人是正直的，但他们却寻找许多计策。”

paintings.title: bread with joy
paintings.epigraph: “eat your bread with joy, and drink your wine with a merry heart; for God has already accepted your works.”
paintings.poem:
go. eat your bread.
drink your wine.

put on something white.
put a little oil
in your hair.

this from the man
who called everything
breath.

he knew
how short it was.

that's why he said
don't waste the table.

God has already
accepted your works.

you can sit down now.
paintings.reflectionPrompt: Every stop on the Pilgrim Walk shows how God meets us in ordinary places (Ecclesiastes 9:7–8)—where in your own home or work today does “God has already accepted your works. you can sit down now” ring true?
paintings.zh_poem:
走吧。吃你的面包。
喝你的酒。

穿上白色的东西。
放少许油
在你的头发里。

这是来自男人的
谁叫一切
呼吸。

他知道
多么短啊。

这就是为什么他说
不要浪费桌子。

神已经
接受了你的作品。

你现在可以坐下了。
paintings.zh_reflectionPrompt: 天路历程中的每一站都展示了神如何在平常的地方与我们相遇（传道书 9:7-8）——今天在你自己的家里或工作场所，“神已经悦纳了你的行为，你现在可以坐下来了”听起来是真的吗？
paintings.zh_epigraph: “要喜乐地吃你的饼，心里快乐地喝你的酒；因为上帝已经悦纳了你的行为。”

paintings.title: with your might
paintings.epigraph: “Whatever your hand finds to do, do it with your might”
paintings.poem:
whatever is in front of you,
the board,
the bread,
the child who needs you,

do it with your might.

he's plain about why:
the day is coming
when there's no more work
to do.

not a threat.
an invitation.

you have hands today.
use them like it matters.

it does.
paintings.reflectionPrompt: Take a slow breath and read the final line again: “use them like it matters. it does.” How would you walk through the next hour differently if you carried that truth with you?
paintings.zh_poem:
无论你面前有什么，
董事会，
面包，
需要你的孩子，

尽你的力量去做吧。

他很清楚为什么：
这一天即将到来
当没有更多工作的时候
去做。

不是威胁。
邀请函。

今天你有手。
像重要的那样使用它们。

确实如此。
paintings.zh_reflectionPrompt: 缓慢地吸一口气，再次阅读最后一行：“像重要的那样使用它们。确实如此。”如果你带着这个真理，你会如何以不同的方式度过接下来的一个小时？
paintings.zh_epigraph: “无论你的手做什么，都要尽力去做”

paintings.title: time and chance
paintings.epigraph: “the race is not to the swift, nor the battle to the strong”
paintings.poem:
the fastest runner stumbles.
the strongest loses.
the wisest man in town
goes without bread.

he doesn't pretend
it's fair.

time and chance
happen to them all.

there's a freedom in that:
you were never
the only one
writing your days.

so run anyway.
just hold the finish line
a little looser.
paintings.reflectionPrompt: Think of a season when you knew the feeling of “the fastest runner stumbles.” Looking through the lens of Ecclesiastes 9:11, what does it mean to discover that “just hold the finish line a little looser”?
paintings.zh_poem:
跑得最快的人也会绊倒。
最强的就输了。
城里最聪明的人
没有面包就去。

他不假装
这是公平的。

时间和机会
发生在他们所有人身上。

这是一种自由：
你从来都不是
唯一的一个
写下你的日子。

所以无论如何都要跑。
只要守住终点线
宽松一点。
paintings.zh_reflectionPrompt: 想象一下您体验过“跑得最快的人跌倒”感觉的一个季节。从传道书 9 章 11 节的角度来看，发现“把终点线放松一点”意味着什么？
paintings.zh_epigraph: “比赛不是跑得快的人，战斗也不是强者的事”

paintings.title: the poor wise man
paintings.epigraph: “yet no man remembered that same poor man.”
paintings.poem:
a little city.
a few people.
a great king outside the walls.

and one poor man
who knew what to do.

he saved them all.

then everyone
went back to their lives
and forgot him.

the Preacher
never gives his name.

but he wrote it down,
and here we are,

remembering
a man
no one remembered.
paintings.reflectionPrompt: Look closely at the stones of the wall in this painting (Ecclesiastes 9:14–15)—if you could leave one anxious weight beside it today, what would you set down?
paintings.zh_poem:
一个小城市。
几个人。
墙外有一位伟大的国王。

和一个穷人
谁知道该怎么做。

他救了他们所有人。

然后大家
回到了他们的生活
并忘记了他。

传教士
从不透露他的名字。

但他写下了，
我们在这里，

回忆
一个男人
没有人记得。
paintings.zh_reflectionPrompt: 仔细观察这幅画中的墙石（传道书 9：14-15）——如果今天你可以在它旁边留下一个令人焦虑的重物，你会放什么？
paintings.zh_epigraph: “然而没有人记得那个可怜的人。”

paintings.title: sharpen the edge
paintings.epigraph: “If the ax is blunt, and one doesn’t sharpen the edge, then he must use more strength; but skill brings success.”
paintings.poem:
you can swing harder.

or you can
sit down a minute
and sharpen the edge.

only a fool
calls that
wasted time.
paintings.reflectionPrompt: Let your eyes rest on the brushwork and light around the quiet centerpiece of “sharpen the edge”: what quiet prayer rises in you when you read, “only a fool calls that wasted time”?
paintings.zh_poem:
你可以用力挥杆。

或者你可以
坐下一分钟
并锐化边缘。

只是一个傻瓜
称之为
浪费时间。
paintings.zh_reflectionPrompt: 让你的目光停留在“磨砺边缘”安静的中心周围的笔触和光线上：当你读到“只有傻瓜才认为这是浪费时间”时，你内心会升起什么样的安静祈祷？
paintings.zh_epigraph: “斧头钝了，不磨刃，就必须用更多的力量；但技巧会带来成功。”

paintings.title: cast your bread
paintings.epigraph: “Cast your bread on the waters; for you shall find it after many days.”
paintings.poem:
let it go.

the kindness
you can't track.
the gift
no one thanked you for.
the seed
you'll never see sprout.

send it out on the water.
don't chase it down the shore.

after many days,
he says,
you'll find it.

he doesn't say where.

he doesn't say
it will look
the way it left.
paintings.reflectionPrompt: Linger with the movement in “cast your bread” (Ecclesiastes 11:1) from “let it go. the kindness you can't track” to “he doesn't say it will look the way it left”—where do you find yourself along that arc today?
paintings.zh_poem:
放手吧。

善良
你无法追踪。
礼物
没有人感谢你。
种子
你永远看不到发芽。

将其发送到水面上。
不要把它追到岸边。

许多天后，
他说，
你会找到的。

他没有说在哪里。

他没有说
它会看起来
它离开的方式。
paintings.zh_reflectionPrompt: 留心“把你的面包撒在地上”（传道书 11:1）中的运动，从“让它过去吧。你无法追寻的恩慈”到“他没有说它会像原来那样”——今天你发现自己处于这条弧线的哪个位置？
paintings.zh_epigraph: “把你的面包撒在水面上；因为很多天之后你就会找到它。”

paintings.title: sow in the morning
paintings.epigraph: “In the morning sow your seed, and in the evening don’t withhold your hand”
paintings.poem:
wait for the wind to settle
and you'll never sow.
wait for the perfect sky
and you'll never reap.

you don't know
the way of the wind.
you don't know
how bones grow
in the womb.

you don't know
which seed
will come up.

so sow in the morning.
sow in the evening.

leave the rest
to the one
who does know.
paintings.reflectionPrompt: Notice how “sow in the morning” (Ecclesiastes 11:4–6) arrives at: “leave the rest to the one who does know.” Who in your life is walking a hard stretch of road today and needs you to share this grace with them?
paintings.zh_poem:
等待风停
你永远不会播种。
等待完美的天空
而你永远不会有收获。

你不知道
风之道。
你不知道
骨头如何生长
在子宫里。

你不知道
哪个种子
会出现。

所以早上播种。
晚上播种。

留下剩下的
给一个
谁知道呢。
paintings.zh_reflectionPrompt: 请注意“早晨撒种”（传道书 11：4-6）如何演变为：“剩下的留给知道的人”。今天，你生命中的哪些人正走在艰难的道路上，需要你与他们分享这份恩典？
paintings.zh_epigraph: “早上播种，晚上不要缩手”

paintings.title: the light is sweet
paintings.epigraph: “Truly the light is sweet, and it is a pleasant thing for the eyes to see the sun.”
paintings.poem:
after all his hard words,
this:

the light is sweet.

it's good
just to see the sun.

he knows
the dark days
will be many.
he says that too.

but he won't let them
spoil the morning.

open the shutters.
sit in it.

it's allowed.
paintings.reflectionPrompt: What if the most important thing you remember before tonight is the quiet lesson of Ecclesiastes 11:7–8: “open the shutters. sit in it. it's allowed”?
paintings.zh_poem:
在他说了这么多严厉的话之后
这个：

光线是甜蜜的。

很好
只是为了看到太阳。

他知道
黑暗的日子
会很多。
他也这么说。

但他不会让他们
破坏早晨。

打开百叶窗。
坐在里面。

这是允许的。
paintings.zh_reflectionPrompt: 如果今晚之前你记得的最重要的事情是《传道书》11:7-8 的安静教训：“打开百叶窗。坐在里面。这是允许的”怎么办？
paintings.zh_epigraph: “光确实很甜蜜，看到太阳的眼睛真是一件令人愉快的事情。”

paintings.title: rejoice in your youth
paintings.epigraph: “Rejoice, young man, in your youth, and let your heart cheer you in the days of your youth”
paintings.poem:
run.
laugh.
follow your heart
out into the morning.

he means it.

and in the same breath
he says:
God will bring you
into judgment.

he isn't taking back
the joy.

he's making sure
it's the kind
you'll still be glad of
later.
paintings.reflectionPrompt: Imagine standing inside this frame beside the quiet rhythm of your breath: what hurry or noise in your week begins to fade when you hear, “he's making sure it's the kind you'll still be glad of later”?
paintings.zh_poem:
跑。
笑。
跟随你的心
一直到早上。

他是认真的。

同时
他说：
神会带你来
进入判断。

他不会收回
喜悦。

他正在确保
就是那种
你仍然会感到高兴
稍后。
paintings.zh_reflectionPrompt: 想象一下，站在这个框架内，旁边是你安静的呼吸节奏：当你听到“他正在确保这是你以后仍然会感到高兴的那种”时，你一周中的什么匆忙或噪音开始消失？
paintings.zh_epigraph: “年轻人，在你的青春里欢欣鼓舞，在你的青春岁月里让你的心为你欢呼”

paintings.title: remember
paintings.epigraph: “Remember also your Creator in the days of your youth, before the evil days come”
paintings.poem:
remember him
now,

while the sun
is still bright,
before the clouds
come back after the rain,

while it's easy
to kneel
and easy
to rise.

not because
he'll forget you later.

because you'll want
to know the way home
by heart
before the lights
begin to dim.
paintings.reflectionPrompt: Read the closing words aloud in the stillness: “because you'll want to know the way home by heart before the lights begin to dim.” What part of your heart feels most searched or comforted by Ecclesiastes 12:1–2 right now?
paintings.zh_poem:
记住他
现在，

当太阳
依然明亮，
云彩之前
雨后回来，

虽然这很容易
跪下
和容易
上升。

不是因为
他以后会忘记你的。

因为你会想要
知道回家的路
用心
灯光前
开始变暗。
paintings.zh_reflectionPrompt: 在寂静中大声朗读结束语：“因为在灯光开始变暗之前，你会想记住回家的路。”现在，传道书 12：1-2 给你心灵的哪一部分带来最深刻的审视或安慰？
paintings.zh_epigraph: “在你年轻的时候，在邪恶的日子到来之前，也要记住你的创造者”

paintings.title: the almond tree
paintings.epigraph: “the almond tree shall blossom”
paintings.poem:
he paints old age
like a house
going quiet.

the hands tremble.
the grinding stops.
the windows dim.
the doors close to the street.

you wake at the voice of a bird.
the songs grow soft.

and out on the hill
the almond tree
blossoms white.

every house
goes quiet someday.

the tree
still blooms.
paintings.reflectionPrompt: In Ecclesiastes 12:3–5, grace meets us right beside the open threshold: how does the closing thought—“and out on the hill the almond tree blossoms white. the tree still blooms”—steady your footing for the road ahead?
paintings.zh_poem:
他画老年
像房子一样
安静下来。

双手颤抖。
研磨停止。
窗户昏暗。
门靠近街道。

你在鸟鸣声中醒来。
歌曲变得柔和。

在山上
杏仁树
花白色。

每个房子
总有一天会安静下来。

树
仍然盛开。
paintings.zh_reflectionPrompt: 在传道书 12:3-5 中，恩典就在敞开的门槛旁与我们相遇：最后的思想——“山上杏树开花白了。树仍然开花”——如何为你前面的路站稳脚跟？
paintings.zh_epigraph: “杏树将会开花”

paintings.title: the silver cord
paintings.epigraph: “before the silver cord is severed, or the golden bowl is broken”
paintings.poem:
a silver cord.
a golden bowl.
a pitcher at the spring.
a wheel at the cistern.

lovely things, and breakable.

one day the cord lets go,
the bowl falls,
the pitcher breaks,

and the dust goes back
to the earth it came from.

but that isn't
where the sentence ends:

the spirit returns
to God who gave it.

you were lent.
you are expected.
paintings.reflectionPrompt: If today’s painting of “the silver cord” (Ecclesiastes 12:6–7) hung beside the door you walk out of this morning, how would its final line—“you were lent. you are expected”—shape your choices?
paintings.zh_poem:
一根银线。
一个金碗。
泉边的一个投手。
水箱里的一个轮子。

可爱的东西，而且易碎。

有一天，绳子松了，
碗掉下来，
投手破裂，

尘埃归去
到它所来自的地球。

但那不是
句子结束的地方：

精神回归
献给赐予它的上帝。

你被借给了。
你是被期待的。
paintings.zh_reflectionPrompt: 如果今天早上你走出的门旁挂着今天的“银线”（传道书 12：6-7）画作，那么它的最后一行——“你是借给你的。你是被期待的”——会如何影响你的选择？
paintings.zh_epigraph: “银线未断，金碗未碎”

paintings.title: the end of the matter
paintings.epigraph: “Fear God and keep his commandments; for this is the whole duty of man.”
paintings.poem:
of making many books,
he says, there is no end.

(this one included.)

and much study
wears you out.

so here is
the end of the matter:

fear God.
keep his commandments.

not a small life.
a whole one.

everything else
is breath.

this
is what breath
is for.
paintings.reflectionPrompt: Every stop on the Pilgrim Walk shows how God meets us in ordinary places (Ecclesiastes 12:12–13)—where in your own home or work today does “this is what breath is for” ring true?
paintings.zh_poem:
制作许多书籍，
他说，没有尽头。

（包括这个。）

和大量的学习
让你疲惫不堪。

所以这是
事情的结局：

敬畏上帝。
遵守他的诫命。

不是一个小生命。
一整个。

其他一切
是呼吸。

这个
是什么呼吸
是为了.
paintings.zh_reflectionPrompt: 天路历程中的每一站都展示了神如何在平常的地方与我们相遇（传道书 12：12-13）——今天，在你自己的家里或工作场所，“这就是呼吸的作用”听起来是真实的吗？
paintings.zh_epigraph: “敬畏上帝，遵守他的诫命；因为这是人类的全部职责。”

zh_title: 将永恒安置在世人心里
zh_beforeYouBegin:
传道书以一个词开始，重复了两遍：虚荣、呼吸，然后仔细审视一个人可能追逐的一切：花园和水池、银子和金子、智慧本身。其间：风吹过，河水汇入永不满溢的大海，哭泣的时刻和跳舞的时刻，三重绳索，撒在水面上的面包，开花的杏树，银绳和金碗。

本书分为四部分，共三十六首短诗。每首诗都位于一幅画旁边和一行经文之下。这些图片与传教士注意到的东西在一起——一盏刚刚吹灭的灯、一堆田野里的石头、一条面包和一个杯子——把面孔留给你想象。

这些诗不是圣经。它们是一位读者对此的回应。打开这本书旁边的传道书，让真实的话语成为最后的话语。
